images.title: The 1917 draft lottery
images.description: The July 1917 draft lottery, where drawn numbers decided who went to France; 24 million registered, 2.8 million drafted.

images.title: A 1917 draft registration card
images.description: A World War I draft registration card, the paperwork behind the 24 million men who registered under the Selective Service Act.

images.title: New York Draft Riots, 1863
images.description: A Civil War draft office, the contrast the script draws: in 1863 a three-hundred-dollar payment bought your way out; in 1917 rich and poor drew from one pool.

images.title: Trench warfare drill, Camp Meade
images.description: American soldiers training in 1917, the army of millions that needed food, uniforms, rifles, and ships from a Washington that had never run an economy at this scale.

images.title: Women munitions workers, 1917
images.description: A munitions factory in 1917, the industrial mobilization the War Industries Board was created to steer.

images.title: Bernard Baruch, head of the War Industries Board
images.description: Portrait of Bernard Baruch, who ran the War Industries Board, setting priorities, nudging prices, and rationing steel and copper.

images.title: War Industries Board, 1917
images.description: A War Industries Board meeting in 1918; Princeton's review calls its record 'mixed': big, slow, inefficient.

images.title: Inside Bethlehem Steel Works
images.description: A steel plant in 1917, the raw materials — steel and copper — that Baruch's board rationed.

images.title: Herbert Hoover, head of the Food Administration
images.description: Herbert Hoover as head of the U.S. Food Administration, which skipped ration books and ran on voluntary pledges.

images.title: 'Food Will Win the War' poster
images.description: The Food Administration's 'Food Will Win the War' poster, its wartime slogan for the voluntary conservation campaign.

images.title: Food Administration poster for immigrants
images.description: A Food Administration poster urging immigrants to conserve food: 'You came here seeking freedom. You must now help to preserve it.'

images.title: Food Administration anti-waste poster
images.description: A 'Meatless Mondays' poster from the Food Administration's voluntary pledge campaign.

images.title: Teaching food conservation canning, 1917
images.description: A family canning vegetables in 1917, the home-front conservation Hoover's pledges asked for.

images.title: Third Liberty Loan poster
images.description: A Third Liberty Loan poster; the four wartime drives raised about seventeen billion dollars.

images.title: Fourth Liberty Loan poster, 1918
images.description: A Fourth Liberty Loan poster from 1918, the last of the four drives that paid roughly two-thirds of the war's cost.

images.title: 'Clear the Way!! Buy Bonds' poster
images.description: 'Clear the Way!! Buy Bonds,' a Fourth Liberty Loan poster from the quota races between cities.

images.title: Liberty Bond rally
images.description: A Liberty Loan rally in 1918, the bond drives that were among the first national ad campaigns in American history.

images.title: Movie stars at a Liberty Loan rally
images.description: Charlie Chaplin pitching Liberty Bonds, the celebrity pitches Madison Avenue borrowed the playbook from.

images.title: George Creel, head of the Committee on Public Information
images.description: Portrait of George Creel, the journalist who ran the Committee on Public Information, created in 1917 to sell the war.

images.title: Four-Minute Men marching, Pennsylvania
images.description: Four-Minute Men marching in Pennsylvania; about seventy-five thousand volunteers gave short patriotic speeches in theaters, churches, and schools.

images.title: 'I Want You for U.S. Army' by James Montgomery Flagg, 1917
images.description: James Montgomery Flagg's 1917 'I Want You for U.S. Army' poster, the pointing Uncle Sam of Maya's childhood.

images.title: 'Destroy This Mad Brute: Enlist' poster, 1917
images.description: Harry R. Hopps's 1917 'Destroy This Mad Brute: Enlist' poster, the gorilla in a German helmet that turned the enemy into a monster.

images.title: Navy recruiting poster by Howard Chandler Christy, 1917
images.description: Howard Chandler Christy's 1917 Navy recruiting poster: 'Gee!! I wish I were a man — I'd join the Navy.'

images.title: 'Tell That to the Marines' poster
images.description: An anti-'Hun' propaganda poster, the ugliest of the CPI's output, turning German soldiers into cartoon monsters.

images.title: John Meintz, a German-American punished in WWI
images.description: A German-American family in 1917, caught in the fear the propaganda unleashed in daily life.

images.title: A 1917 passenger station
images.description: Black Southerners boarding a northbound train during the Great Migration; more than half a million left the South during the war years.

images.title: Packard factory, Detroit
images.description: African American migrants arriving in Chicago in 1917, drawn by factory jobs and wages unreachable in Mississippi.

images.title: Fire during the East St. Louis riot, July 1917
images.description: Fire during the July 1917 East St. Louis race riot, where the official count says thirty-nine Black and nine white people were killed.

images.title: The NAACP's Silent Protest Parade, July 1917
images.description: The NAACP's Silent Protest Parade down Fifth Avenue on July 28, 1917, answering the East St. Louis violence.

images.title: American women munitions workers, World War I
images.description: American women munitions workers in World War I; the work was visible and patriotic, and that visibility became leverage for the vote.

images.title: Women munition workers demand suffrage, 1917
images.description: Women office workers in 1917, the new wartime workforce that turned visibility into suffrage leverage.

images.title: Women's agricultural work, 1917
images.description: Women farm workers in 1917, filling the labor gap the war opened in the fields as well as the factories.

images.title: Alice Paul, 1915
images.description: Alice Paul in 1915; she founded the National Woman's Party in 1916 and picketed the White House before the war touched American soil.

images.title: Silent Sentinels picketing the White House
images.description: National Woman's Party Silent Sentinels picketing the White House, the radical tactics behind the suffrage leverage.

images.title: Carrie Chapman Catt, NAWSA president
images.description: Carrie Chapman Catt, president of NAWSA, which counted over two million members by 1917 after decades of organizing.

images.title: Woodrow Wilson leaving the White House
images.description: Wilson addressing the Senate in September 1918, backing a federal suffrage amendment in pure war logic: 'partners of the women in this war.'

images.title: The Schenck anti-draft leaflet
images.description: The anti-draft leaflet at the center of Schenck v. United States, the 1919 case that drew the 'clear and present danger' line.

images.title: Justice Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr.
images.description: Portrait of Justice Oliver Wendell Holmes, who wrote that free speech doesn't protect a man 'falsely shouting fire in a theatre.'

images.title: Eugene V. Debs
images.description: Eugene V. Debs, the Socialist leader sentenced to ten years for a 1918 speech, then run for president from a federal prison cell.

images.title: Debs speaking in Canton, Ohio, 1918
images.description: Debs speaking in Canton, Ohio in 1918, the speech that earned him ten years under the Espionage Act.

images.title: The Atlanta federal penitentiary, 1920
images.description: The Atlanta federal penitentiary, where Debs sat in 1920 while winning roughly 913,000 votes for president.

images.title: Warren G. Harding
images.description: Portrait of Warren G. Harding, who commuted Debs's sentence; Debs walked out of prison on Christmas Day, 1921.

images.title: The Big Four at Paris, 1919
images.description: Wilson in 1919, the president who refused to pardon Debs despite the pleas.

images.title: The Alien and Sedition Acts, 1798
images.description: The text of the Alien and Sedition Acts of 1798, the first instance of the wartime civil-liberties pattern the script traces.

images.title: Abraham Lincoln, 1863
images.description: Lincoln in the Civil War, the second instance: suspending habeas corpus, the pattern's middle case.

images.title: Japanese American internment, World War II
images.description: Japanese American internment in World War II, the pattern's later instance: wartime fear shrinking what Americans could say and be.

images.title: Men waiting to enlist, 1917
images.description: A 1917 enlistment line, the volunteers the posters and the Four-Minute Men were selling the war to.

images.title: Red Cross poster, 1917
images.description: Red Cross volunteers rolling bandages in 1917, the home-front mobilization beyond the factories.

images.title: Public school war garden, 1917
images.description: A public school war garden — the Food Administration's home-front campaign.

images.title: Women practicing voting, Dayton, 1920
images.description: Women practicing voting in Dayton, 1920 — the amendment ratified.

images.title: 'Cabins for Colored' (segregation)
images.description: 'Cabins for Colored' — the Jim Crow South migrants fled.

images.title: Women's Suffrage Parade, 1917
images.description: The Women's Suffrage Parade, 1917.

images.title: Fourth Liberty Loan workers
images.description: Fourth Liberty Loan workers — the bond drives.

images.title: Boy Scouts, New York City, 1917
images.description: Boy Scouts in New York City, 1917 — the home front mobilized.

images.title: Making uniforms for the war
images.description: Making uniforms for the war — mobilizing the economy.

images.title: Shipyard riveter, September 1917
images.description: A shipyard riveter, September 1917 — building the ships.

images.title: Eugene Debs released from prison, 1921
images.description: Eugene Debs released from prison, 1921 — Harding commuted the sentence.

images.description: 'Halt the Hun' — the anti-German propaganda.

images.description: Women workers in a shoe factory — the war industries.
